sources.title: SRCDS.py - HL1/HL2 RCON library: HL1 auth via 'challenge rcon' over UDP; banid <minutes> <steamid> + writeid; removeid <steamid> + writeid; say; status; swaps the name/userid header keys on HL1
Valve Developer Community console command list - kick 'Kick a player by slot, userid or name'; banid 'Add a user ID to the ban list'; removeid 'Remove a user ID from the ban list'
Valve hlds mailing list - ban list is loaded into memory from banned.cfg and edited with addid/removeid
MultiModServer issue #46 - real GoldSrc status capture: header '#      name userid uniqueid frag time ping loss adr', rows '# 1 "<name>" 550 BOT 0 11:51:08 0 0'
node-rcon - protocol table: 'Any GoldSrc game | UDP | Yes (challenge)' vs 'Any Source game | TCP | N/A'
SteamDB app 90 - Half-Life Dedicated Server (Tool, GoldSource)

notes: Condition Zero is a GoldSrc mod: the server binary is Half-Life Dedicated Server (Steam app 90, confirmed by LinuxGSM) run with mod dir 'czero'; the game's own app id is 80. App 90 is SHARED with CS 1.6, DoD and every other HL1 mod, so appId alone cannot identify a CZ server - the mod dir is what distinguishes it, and the generic alias 'Half-Life Dedicated Server' is deliberately NOT listed here because it would match those other mods' files too. GoldSrc RCON is Valve's older UDP challenge-response protocol on the game port, NOT Source TCP RCON, hence flavour 'custom'; node-rcon's protocol table and SRCDS.py's 'challenge rcon' handshake agree. It is enabled purely by setting a non-empty rcon_password - no enable setting, no separate RCON port (it rides the UDP game port, default 27015). status is both info and roster; a real GoldSrc capture (MultiModServer #46) shows header '#      name userid uniqueid frag time ping loss adr' with rows '# <slot> "<name>" <userid> <uniqueid> ...', i.e. the name precedes the userid, the reverse of Source. SRCDS.py corroborates by swapping those two header keys on its HL1 branch. Bots and LAN clients print BOT or VALVE_ID_LAN in the uniqueid column and are dropped by linePattern. kick is written against {playerName} because Valve's command list documents kick as taking a slot, userid or name and GoldSrc has no kickid; note that AMX Mod X itself only ever emits the 'kick #<userid>' form, so the quoted-name form is documented rather than observed in that code - the userid is captured as accountId so a caller can use 'kick #<userid>' instead. banid takes MINUTES FIRST then the Steam ID (0 = permanent) and does NOT reliably disconnect an already-connected player: AMX Mod X always issues a kick alongside it and so should the runtime. writeid flushes the in-memory list to czero/banned.cfg; the 'wait' between banid and writeid is copied verbatim from AMX Mod X, which inserts it deliberately. removeid is chained with writeid and NO wait, again matching AMX Mod X exactly. There is no motd command - the MOTD is the file czero/motd.txt. Correction to an earlier draft of this file: developer.valvesoftware.com is reachable and was read for this entry; the previous claim that it returned HTTP 403 to every attempt was wrong.
